title: Build a 4-bit adder with carry
statement_md: Create a combinational module named `adder4`. Inputs `a` and `b` are 4 bits each and `cin` is the carry-in. Output `sum` holds the low 4 bits of `a + b + cin` and `cout` holds the carry-out.

ports.name: sum
ports.desc: Low 4 bits of a + b + cin

sample_tests.expected: sum contains the 4-bit result; cout=0 unless overflow

tests.hint: Check plain addition without any carry involved.
cin must be added into the result, not ignored.

tests.purpose: wraps 15 + 1 to 0 and sets the carry
tests.hint: The sum needs 5 bits internally, so 15 + 1 must give sum=0 and cout=1.
15 + 15 + 1 = 31, which needs 5 bits; sum holds the lower 4, cout holds the 5th.
9 + 7 = 16 exactly. Check that it sets cout without leaving a stale value in sum.

hints: The full result of a + b + cin can need 5 bits. Give it somewhere to go.
Concatenating {cout, sum} on the left of one assignment sizes the result for you.
Remember that cin is part of the addition, not a separate case.
